sources.title: MCP 2026-07-28 Authorization Security Considerations

sources.title: Claude Agent SDK permission evaluation and approval input updates
supports: Several earlier permission stages may resolve a call before canUseTool.
Callback may approve with modified effective input; it may also persist suggested permission updates.
limitations: Dynamic pages have no stable publication date in the inspected body; access date only.

sources.title: Claude Code custom subagents: permissions, dedicated tools and output authority
locators: Restrict which tools a subagent can use (web lines 452-483)
Scope MCP servers to a subagent (web lines 513-542)
supports: A child can be configured with MCP servers unavailable in the main conversation, while managed restrictions still apply.
Tool access and permission-mode inheritance are distinct mechanisms with documented exceptions.
A subagent report's instruction/approval claims have no user authority; scanning does not replace permission checks or sandboxing.
limitations: Not evidence that every child authority is a subset of the parent's visible tool list.
Our delegation algebra and result recipient controls are proposed application contracts, not stated as implemented Claude semantics.
No attack payloads collected or tested.

our_proposals_not_source_claims: Usable_L(t,q,n) with scoped consumer, operation and recipients.
Artifact materialization separate from access revocation and evidence withdrawal.
Delegated effective scope bounded by parent delegable scope and current policy; separate CanDelegate from CanExecute.
Explicit derived-result release decisions and separate consume/evidence-read/revalidation permissions.
Application approval binding to final effective action, actor, recipients, executor scope and policy dependencies.
Fifteen proposed contract cases; none executed.
uncertainty: Derived-data release invalidation policy remains a business design decision.
Whether any adapter can meet execution-point revocation must be verified independently.
A provenance/taint label is not a proof of model semantic non-disclosure.
